title: Veterans Pension Care Level and Dependent Terms Table
content:
# Care level and dependent terms — Veterans Pension

## Physician's examination report

| Rate category | Physician's examination report required for the rate |
|---|---|
| Veterans Pension (Basic Rate, No Dependents) | No |
| Veterans Pension (Basic Rate, One Dependent) | No |
| Veterans Pension (Housebound, No Dependents) | Yes |
| Veterans Pension (Housebound, One Dependent) | Yes |
| Veterans Pension (Aid and Attendance, No Dependents) | Yes |
| Veterans Pension (Aid and Attendance, One Dependent) | Yes |

## Figures common to every rate category

| Term | Value |
|---|---|
| Rating of the single permanent disability for housebound status | 100 percent |
| Rating of the separate disability that, with the single 100 percent disability, establishes housebound status | 60 percent |
| A veteran meeting aid-and-attendance criteria is paid at the aid-and-attendance rate rather than housebound | Yes |
| Moving from a no-dependent to a one-dependent rate requires a dependency claim received online or by mail | Yes |
| Days after a marriage or birth within which a dependency claim takes the event date as its effective date | 365 calendar days |
| Age at which a child stops counting as a dependent unless in school or helpless | 18 years |
| Age at which a child attending school stops counting as a dependent | 23 years |

## Boundary illustrations (hypothetical)

- A separate disability rated 60 percent alongside a single permanent 100 percent disability meets the housebound figures; a separate disability rated 50 percent does not meet the 60 percent figure.
- A dependency claim received 365 days after a birth is within the window; one received 366 days after is outside it.
- A child not in school stops counting at the 18th birthday; a child in school stops counting at the 23rd birthday.
